scope: Fix lower side trim intersecting tyres and longitudinal hub drift on inclines; preserve existing low-poly silhouettes and dynamics calibration.
rootCauses: Batched side skirts and SUV rocker cladding were sized from overall vehicle length instead of the interval between tyre/arch envelopes.
fixedFootprintWheelZ moved the local wheel pivot longitudinally to keep an unpitched world footprint, separating hubs from wheel arches when chassis pitch changed.
A vehicle swap on a grade initialized chassis pitch at zero, transiently lifting an axle before road-pitch smoothing settled.
fixes: Shorten the exported mesh islands between existing arch envelopes; update Blender authoring source and preserve all triangles/materials/rigs.
Keep authored local axle Z fixed, solve local suspension Y against re-sampled pitched world footprints, and compute bump-stop chassis height in the same coordinates.
Include circular tread and tyre width support against local road slope, while retaining analytic kerb-volume resistance and sidewall blocking.
Initialize newly spawned/replaced car pitch from its support plane.
Expose uphill/downhill grade inspection points in the normal T panel.

automated.fullSuite: npm test passed; subsequently expanded actual-tyre obstacle regression from two cars to all five, which also passed.
automated.kerb: Five GLBs × 5 approach/steer cases × 4 frame rates (15/30/60/120 Hz), actual exported tyre vertices checked against solid kerbs on every frame; energy loss, reverse, weak-drive blocking and roof-roll signs passed.

manual: Blender rendered and visually inspected side views of all five repaired vehicle assets.
In-app browser reloaded the exported assets; all five cars inspected from left side at the approximately 22 degree mountain slope.
N90 inspected in both directions on the same grade; slope throttle/brake interaction exercised, with all four settled contacts reporting zero support gap.
N90 one-side kerb: left/right suspension offset +1.30/-1.30 game units, four grounded contacts and zero support gaps; both visible tyre openings remain clear of rocker ends.
N90 driven forwards over the front-axle kerb contact and stopped with rear axle still approaching; independent dynamic mesh tests cover the complete crossing.
limitations: Contact model remains upright rigid tyres and one suspension translation per wheel, not a fully articulated multi-link or deformable-tyre simulation.

The automated grade sweep covers planar slopes up to plus/minus 35 degrees; the manual slope is about 22 degrees. This does not certify every possible off-road terrain crease or extreme roll/impact state.
No change to vehicle power calibration or guarantee of hill-start capability at the existing limited throttle settings.
